page: Microsoft Azure M64bds_1_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-intensive workloads that require large RAM footprints and local solid-state storage. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at up to 4.0 GHz. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. Memory capacity is substantial at 1,397.0 GB of RAM, equating to 21.83 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as 3,221 GB of fast local SSD, while accelerated graphics processing is absent with a GPU count of 0.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational, memory, and transactional throughput. In Geekbench tests, the server logged a single-core score of 2,166.0 and a multi-core score of 19,691.0, reflecting top 25% performance, with image processing testing reaching top 10% tiers (18,639.0). PassMark scores corroborated this with a total CPU score of 66,425.61 and database operations posting 28,843.47. In memory-intensive evaluations, the instance showed solid bandwidth, logging 4,519.69 GB/sec in small cached block reads and 216.95 GB/sec in 256 MB uncached reads. Redis operations were measured at 70.71 million SET operations per second, supported by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 344.01 GB/sec.

The instance delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for scenarios requiring high memory-to-core ratios and high-density transactional processing without dedicating resources to unneeded GPU hardware. While raw stress-ng compute tests fall into average mid-tier percentiles and CPU-only LLM text generation on large 70B models is restricted (2.58 tokens/sec), the inclusion of 3,221 GB local SSD alongside dense RAM reduces external block storage overhead for temporary files, cache layers, and swap space.

Microsoft Azure M64bds_1_v3 is best suited for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, Redis caching layers, high-throughput database systems, and heavy ETL or data transformation workloads requiring extensive memory allocations and fast local scratch storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top 25% for PassMark CPU metrics (66,425.61) and Geekbench multi-core performance (19,691.0), as well as database operations (28,843.47) and Redis performance (70.71 million SET operations/sec). Memory bandwidth is also pronounced, delivering 216.95 GB/sec in uncached read operations. The server offers cost-efficient scaling for workloads bound by memory volume rather than raw vector graphics processing, making it well matched for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, and memory-heavy transactional processing.
